item.title: Six U.S. agencies finalized GENIUS Act stablecoin rules by the July 18 deadline, setting reserve, audit, and supervisory standards.
U.S. CBDC prohibition took effect July 10, barring the Federal Reserve from issuing a retail digital dollar.
EU MiCA enforcement is live: CASPs without authorization now face penalties of up to 15 million euros per violation.
SEC placed three crypto rulemakings on its July 2026 agenda, with final rules expected no earlier than mid-2027.
Senate Republicans unveiled the CLARITY Act to establish a comprehensive U.S. digital asset regulatory framework.
Three DeFi exploits on July 23 totaled $35.55 million in losses; AFX Trade lost $24 million via a cross-chain bridge flaw.
BlackRock, Coinbase, and Fidelity joined a $15 million Bitcoin Security Consortium on July 23 to fund quantum-resistance research.
BIS warned that USD stablecoins can circumvent capital controls more effectively than foreign-currency bank deposits.
Morgan Stanley filed amended S-1s for spot ether and solana ETFs on July 14, naming Coinbase as custodian at a 0.14% sponsor fee.
U.S. spot ether ETFs attracted $196.4 million in net inflows July 14-21, breaking an eight-week withdrawal streak.
The UK softened draft stablecoin rules but retained single-issuer caps that analysts say may limit market scale.
The SEC agreed July 22 to pay $150,000 and release internal Ethereum communications, settling a FOIA lawsuit.
Crypto hacks reached $1.3 billion in H1 2026 with attackers targeting fewer protocols but extracting larger sums per incident.
TRON was added to the S&P Pantera Digital Asset Index, expanding institutional benchmarks to additional blockchain networks.
